_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); machinery and engines signals

pit_profile.why: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2010 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by higher unemployment, lower consumer spending, lower corporate earnings and lower levels of government and business investment.' and 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our machines and engines.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: 'Caterpillar is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives' (FY2010 10-K, Item 1); 'Caterpillar products and product support services are sold worldwide into a variety of highly competitive markets'; 'The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical and can be significantly reduced in an economic environment characterized by higher unemployment, lower consumer spending, lower corporate earnings and lower levels of government and business investment.' and 'The energy and mining industries are major users of our machines and engines.' (Item 1A): the 10-K calls the demand for its own products cyclical (BKR's 'Our business is cyclical'), so CYCLICAL from the FY2010 10-K; no disruption theme is live for it. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.61x; +10% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +2.05; conservative 2yr +92%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -61.5%/yr (worst year FY01-FY10, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +34.6%/yr (FY11 guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +34.6%/yr (FY01-FY10 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +60.9%/yr (best 2-yr run FY01-FY10); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: CAT (retrospective, 2011-09-02) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.61x (87.1% downside to Bear $11 / +143.6% upside to Bull $208) | Adj composite 3.68 vs market 1.63: gap +2.05 [UNDERVALUED] | +9% above the EPP floor $78 (12x FY11E $6.50) | Conservative 2-yr case: +91.8% total (+45.9%/yr) | At 13.1x FY11E the 15% hurdle price $113 sits at or below the BASE case; Machinery sales +48.5% in Q2 2011, forward revenues +31.5-36.2% (FY11 sales and revenues guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K, Item 8.01: the FY2008-FY2010 financial statements recast for the 2011 segments (Exhibit 99.2)
sources.supports: Five-year Financial Summary 2006-2010 and Results of Operations 2008-2010 as recast (unchanged; 2009 profit per share $2.18 excluding redundancy costs); external sales of Construction Industries $13,572M, Resource Industries $8,667M, Power Systems $15,537M and the Financial Products Segment $2,946M in 2010 ($8,507M, $5,857M, $13,389M and $3,139M in 2009)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: fourth-quarter 2010 results release
sources.supports: fourth-quarter and full-year 2010 sales by geographic region and statement of results; 2009 profit per share $2.18 excluding redundancy costs; 2011 outlook: sales and revenues to exceed $50 billion, profit near $6.00 per share

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: first-quarter 2011 results release
sources.supports: first-quarter 2011 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2011 outlook: sales and revenues $52 to $54 billion, profit $6.25 to $6.75 per share

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: second-quarter 2011 results release
sources.supports: second-quarter 2011 sales and revenues by segment and statement of results; 2011 outlook including Bucyrus: sales and revenues $56 to $58 billion, profit $6.25 to $6.75 per share ($54 to $56 billion and $6.75 to $7.25 excluding it)

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: third-quarter 2010 results release
sources.supports: third-quarter 2010 sales by geographic region and statement of results; 2010 outlook: sales and revenues $41 to $42 billion, profit $3.80 to $4.00 per share; preliminary 2011 sales and revenues approaching $50 billion

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: June 2011 dividend declaration (Exhibit 99.1)
sources.supports: a quarterly cash dividend of $0.46 per share, payable August 20, 2011

sources.title: Caterpillar 8-K: 'Caterpillar Splits Stock; Increases Dividend Rate'
sources.supports: a two-for-one stock split; the split shares distributed on July 13 to stockholders of record on June 22, 2005
